title: Half-day safety buffers and memory ramps log
summary: Personal scratchpad for very short-window releases where latency spikes are common. Emphasis on half-day (6-12 hour) warmups, memory ramping on hosts, and quick safety buffers to avoid noisy rollouts.
content:
Context and intent:
- Short morning releases (06:00-12:00 PT) where customer traffic has a predictable lull but risk of network noise exists later in the window.
- Goal: get a small feature out with minimal blast radius while avoiding OOM/GC thundering in newly scaled pods.
- This is a personal checklist / quick log — keep raw and actionable.

Runbook sketch (6-12 hour cadence):
1) Preflight (T-minus 90m)
   - Verify canary image built and sha matches tag (local): `sha256:` 
   - Quick smoke on staging with 10 simulated users (script: tools/smoke-short.sh) — check response time P95 and memory delta.
   - Confirm alerting mute windows for non-critical noise (alert-ios/mute-release-06-12).

2) Warmup - memory ramps (T-minus 60m -> T0)
   - Purpose: avoid sudden memory jumps and cache population causing OOM.
   - Steps:
     * Start 1 host in warmup pool with new image at 1/100 normal traffic (traffic-split = 0.01).
     * After 15m, add second host in warmup pool (traffic-split = 0.02).
     * At 30m, increase warmup pool traffic to 5% total. Monitor memory RSS + GC pauses.
     * At 45m if P95 latency < baseline+25ms and memory steady, add 2 more hosts and increase to 15%.

   - Heuristic thresholds (quick reference):
     * Memory increase per host <= 20% of baseline within first 30m.
     * GC pause 95th < 300ms.
     * Error rate < 0.1% relative to baseline. If any fail, revert host and keep warmup paused.

3) Canary (T0 -> +3h)
   - Start with 1% traffic -> monitor for 30m.
   - If stable, 5% for 60m.
   - If stable, 20% for remaining warm period.
   - If at any point latency or errors jump above thresholds, trigger rollback (see Rollback triggers).

4) Full rollout decision (after +6h steady)
   - Decision checklist:
     * Latency (P95) within +20ms of baseline for 6h.
     * Token-cost per request within expected variance.
     * Ops dashboard (per-route) shows no new spikes in dropped requests or queueing.
     * No new SLO violations recorded.
   - If pass, schedule gradual 24-48h shift to 100% (automated ramp via infra). If borderline, keep at 20-50% and re-evaluate next day.

Quick rollback triggers (auto + manual):
- Auto rollback (immediate): sustained error rate >= 1% for 10m OR latency P95 > baseline + 100ms for 5m.
- Soft rollback (manual alert to on-call): memory per host > baseline * 1.5 OR GC pause 95th > 500ms.
- Manual rollback: any customer-facing functional regression found in prod.

Operational telemetry to watch (dashboard pins):
- per-route P50/P95/P99 latency (3m/15m windows)
- error rate by status code and by route
- host RSS/heap distribution (heatmap) — watch shift in median
- GC pause distribution (p95/p99)
- queue depth for request router and kernel threads
- infra autoscaler events (scale-ups, preemptions)
- model KV cache hit rate (if applicable)
- token-cost burn rate (compare to expected cadence)

Quick commands and notes (cheat sheet):
- Force rollback of tag: `rdctl rollout revert --service X --to-tag stable-2026-02-20`
- Pause warmup pool: `infra warmup set --service X --rate 0` (ops-only)
- Bump GC tuning for hosts in warmup: edit `jvmflags: -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200` in warmup image and retest locally.

Sample compact rollout config (for automation team) - paste into ticket:
- name: short-morning-rollout
  window: 06:00-12:00 PT
  warmup:
    steps: ["0.01 for 15m", "0.02 for 15m", "0.05 for 30m", "0.15 for 15m"]
  canary: ["1% for 30m", "5% for 60m", "20% for remaining warm period"]
  thresholds:
    latency_p95_ms: 100
    error_rate_pct: 0.1
    memory_increase_pct_per_host: 20

Open questions / unresolved bits:
- Are warmup pools billed to customer vs infra budget? Need to confirm with finance for Dedicated customers. (Linked ticket finance#445)
- Should we schedule a short pre-warm at 03:00 for APAC-heavy endpoints? Might avoid morning surges there; need PM input.
- How to test model KV cache cold-start realistically in staging? Current staging usage is too low to reproduce cache miss storms.

Post-release quick log (template, fill immediately after):
- Release tag: 
- Start time: 
- End time: 
- Peak mem delta observed: 
- Max GC p95: 
- Any auto rollbacks? 
- Manual interventions: 
- Notes for next run: 

Personal heuristics / mental checklist while on-call:
- If anything looks trending bad, cut to 0.1% and reassess; lower traffic is reversible and cheap.
- Prefer longer warmup (more gradual) when memory shows even small increases.
- Avoid full 100% flips in same day if any metric was borderline earlier.

References / links to related notes:
- confluence:release-runbook-3 (official runbook)
- ticket: JIRA-8742 (deploy automation tweak for warmup pools)
- slack: #deploy-safety (pinned snippet includes canned rollback commands)

End of scratchpad.

-- Claire
